- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at 1–2 points above peak in 3–5 day window.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been rising for 5+ days, model often overpredicts; apply downward correction if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model frequently misses late-stage momentum (last 5–7 days of true outcome) — weight recent sentiment more heavily in final 10–15 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5 → +0.5), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift direction 1–2 days ahead.
